subject: Meeting invite anchor broken — proposed new demo time and timezone warp fix
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Li <evan@storix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Meeting invite anchor broken — proposed new demo time and timezone warp fix

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for scheduling the demo. A couple of customers on your side flagged that the invite we sent earlier shows a blank join link for some attendees and the time displays as 02:00 on their calendar (they're on CET). I pulled the .ics and it looks like the DTSTART anchor got written with an incorrect TZID which is causing clients to display a shifted time (the classic "timezone-warp" where some clients treat it as UTC).

Can we do two things quickly so we can keep the momentum?

- I attached an updated demo deck for your team to review.
- Proposed workaround: move the demo to one of these slots so we avoid overnight hours for your EU team:
  * Tue Dec 21 — 11:00 AM PT / 7:00 PM CET
  * Tue Dec 21 — 2:00 PM PT / 10:00 PM CET

If one of those works I will send a fresh invite (new .ics) and ask everyone to delete the old event before accepting to prevent double-booking. I can also create a Meet link instead of Zoom if your org blocks Zoom joins via forwarded invites.

Attached: DemoDeck_v2.pdf and a stubbed .ics I'm preparing.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the heads up. I see the original invite in my Google Calendar as 02:00 (which is not right for our EU folks) — I forwarded it to our devops alias and they confirmed the anchor shows Z (UTC) instead of Europe/Paris. That explains why some attendees see a midnight/early morning slot.

Either of the two times you proposed works for our product team; 11:00 AM PT is preferable. We do have a security policy that blocks third-party Zoom links created by external senders in some accounts — so if you can create the invite from a Google Meet link (and send a fresh .ics) that's ideal.

Hi Evan —

I ran into this "TZID lost in translation" bug a few times with larger customers. Quick playbook we use:

1) Create a NEW calendar event from the organizer's Google account (not forwarded .ics). That avoids Zoom-invite sanitizers in Outlook/G Suite.
2) Explicitly set the TZ in the event creation UI (e.g., Europe/Paris) rather than relying on auto-detection.
3) Include both the Meet URL in the body and attach an .ics with the same DTSTART so clients that ingest ICS get a consistent anchor.

If Kimberly can confirm 11:00 AM PT / 7:00 PM CET, I will:
- Generate a Meet-hosted event from our shared redwood.sales@redwood.ai account,
- Attach the updated .ics and check the DTSTART/TZID,
- Post the HubSpot activity link once done so Storix has a single source of truth.

I attached a quick sample .ics we use internally (stub). Also linking the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/54231/detail/DEAL-9982
